- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for next 3–5 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, consider downward bias; reduce by 1–4% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If model forecast is <10% below recent 18-day average, consider upward bias; increase by 1–3% if sentiment is positive or volatile.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from + to - or vice versa) triggers a 2–5% adjustment in forecast direction to align with sentiment shift, especially if price deviates >3% from prior trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; apply a “reversion buffer” — if forecast is >10% above 18-day mean, reduce by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
